title: The LEGO Comeback
short_teaser: A company nearly failed by returning to what made it special.
story: LEGO struggled when it expanded too far away from its core strengths. The company recovered by returning focus to creativity, building, and imagination. A company nearly failed by returning to what made it special. Strategy is not simply making a plan. It is noticing what matters most, choosing where to place effort, learning from evidence, and being willing to adjust before more time or energy is spent. What makes the moment especially useful is the pattern beneath it: attention came before understanding, and understanding came before change. That pattern is available in everyday life too, whenever we resist the urge to dismiss something simply because it does not yet fit the plan. The lasting importance is simple: sometimes growth comes from adding more. Sometimes it comes from returning to what works.
impact: Sometimes growth comes from adding more. Sometimes it comes from returning to what works. A strong strategy reduces noise by helping us choose what deserves attention now and what can wait. This matters because the lesson is transferable. It can help someone recognize a pattern, make a more thoughtful choice, or see possibility where they previously saw only a problem.
spark_application: What part of your business deserves more attention? Identify the decision underneath your current activity. Choose the one next move that would create the clearest useful information. Afterward, save a short note about what you noticed, what surprised you, or what you may want to revisit.
